parts.text: Which claim correctly judges lustre and whether shine proves a metal?

options.text: The copper wire is lustrous; the glitter on the glass bead shines but does not prove the bead is a metal.
The glitter-coated glass bead is a metal because it shines.
The clean copper wire is non-lustrous because metals never shine.
Any dull painted surface is lustrous if the paint looks gold-coloured.

parts.text: Give one reason for your choice.

stem: Kavya holds a clean copper wire and a glass bead coated with glitter glue up to a lamp.

part_answers.answer: Metals such as copper typically look lustrous, but shine alone does not prove a material is a metal — glitter on glass can shine too.

teacher.key_rationale: Lustrous materials usually look shiny and are often metals, but shine is not enough to prove a metal. Glitter on glass can shine without being metal.
